turns.t: Mr Reilly, I wanted to talk about your vitamin D. It came back low. Do you know why you were tested? ~
My wife made me. I'm tired, I guess. For about four months.
Tired how? All day, or at certain times?
All day. I wake up tired.
That's what low vitamin D can do. How's your mood? ~
Fine. Just flat. ~
Are you outdoors much? ~
Not really. I'm at a desk. I leave in the dark, I come home in the dark. ~
That's most of the winter, then. And what do you eat, any fish, eggs? ~
Some eggs. Not much fish. ~
Let me take two quick numbers. Blood pressure 122 over 76, pulse 70.
That's fine? ~
That's fine. Let me press on a few places.
Go ahead. ~
I'm pressing over the shin bone. Any tenderness? ~
A little. Mm. ~
There's mild tenderness over the shin bones, and the muscles of the thighs are slightly sore when I squeeze them.
Yes, my legs ache sometimes. ~
Any numbness or tingling in your hands or feet?
No, nothing like that.
What I think is happening is that low vitamin D could be behind your tiredness, but I can't rule out other causes, so I won't say it's the whole story.
What else could it be? ~
Lots of things cause tiredness, sleep, stress, the winter. But we'll start with the simple fix. ~
What's the fix? ~
More daylight, even in winter. A walk at lunch, for twenty minutes.
I can do that. ~
And eat oily fish, like salmon or mackerel, twice a week, and eggs.
Mackerel. Okay. ~
Keep a note of how your energy is over the next few weeks.
Sure. ~
Any questions for me? ~
Is it serious? ~
Not at all. It's very common, and fixable. ~
Good. I'll tell my wife she was right. ~
She sounds sensible. ~
She is. ~
Anything else on your mind today? ~
No, that's it. Thanks, doctor. ~
